title: Edit Line (Avatar) / Edit 3D Pen (Avatar)
content: ### Objective Edit lines created on an Avatar. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Edit Line (Avatar) / Edit 3D Pen (Avatar) (ver. 2025.0) 3D Toolbar ▶ Edit Line (Avatar) / Edit 3D Pen (Avatar) (ver. 2025.0) ### Operation #### Select/Move 1. Follow the path indicated in the Location section. → If a Garment is on the Avatar, the Garment appears translucent. 2. Click on the line or the shape to be selected. → The line or the shape is selected and highlighted in yellow. 3. While the line of the shape is selected, click and drag to move the selected item to the desired position. #### Delete 1. Follow the path indicated in the Location section. → If a Garment is on the Avatar, the Garment appears translucent. 2. Select the line or the shape to be deleted. 3. Right click on the selected item and select Delete or hit the Delete key on the keyboard. → The selected line or shape is deleted. ※ Note: * To select multiple lines or shapes, hold down the Shift key on the keyboard, then click on additional lines or shapes. * To select all lines and shapes on the Avatar, hit the Ctrl+A on the keyboard. * After the lines and shapes are drawn on the Avatar, if you delete the Avatar, all previously created lines, and shapes are also deleted.
content_description: This webpage provides instructions on how to edit, move, and delete lines and shapes created on an Avatar within the 3D Garment tool.

title: Adjust Avatar Pose
content: ### Objective Adjust poses of avatar with joint information. From ver2.3.0 onwards, it displays sub-groups of avatar joints which enables to see direct groups of joint to be edited. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ Avatar ▶ Show X-ray Joints (Shift + X) / Show Avatar Joints (ver 12) ▶ 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move 3D Window ▶ Avatar Display (Mouse-over) ▶ Show X-ray Joints (Shift + X) / Show Avatar Joints (ver 12) ▶ 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ### Operation #### FK (Forward Kinematics) 1. Follow the path indicated in the Location section. 2. Click on avatar's joint and use Gizmo to relocate and to edit rotation value. Click the 'Symmetric' icon at the top right of the gizmo to apply the rotation value of the joint point in a metric fashion. (ver. 5.1.431) #### IK (Inverse Kinematics) (ver. 2025.0) 1. Follow the path indicated in the Location section. 2. Set Option as needed: **Option** | **Description** ---|--- Edit Full Body | When a single joint is modified, it affects all other joints which are organically linked to the single joint. Edit Body Part | When a single joint is modified, only directly connected joints are modified. Constrain Joint Rotation | Activate the option to prevent unwanted movement of the selected joint caused by other rotating joints. However, for natural modification of the Avatar, the constrained joint may rotate slightly. Constrain Joint Translation | Activate the option to prevent unwanted movement of the selected joint caused by other moving joints. However, for natural modification of the Avatar, the constrained joint may move slightly. 3. Adjust the position and rotation by clicking on the joints in the Gizmo. Joints marked with green dots can be adjusted. Click the symmetry icon on the top right of gizmo to enable symmetric editing.
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for adjusting avatar poses using joint information, featuring enhanced tools for both Forward Kinematics (FK) and Inverse Kinematics (IK) to facilitate precise modifications.

title: Set Graphic Options (Above ver4.2.0)
content: ### Objective Change the default settings of the software menu according to user preference in User Settings. Upon restarting, the user settings of the software becomes the default settings. Shortcut keys, menus, graphic options, view controls, default files, font settings, and other miscellaneous properties can be set in User Settings. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Settings ▶ User Settings ▶ Graphic Options Main Menu ▶ Settings/Preferences ▶ Preferences ▶ Graphic Options (ver 11) Main Menu ▶ Settings ▶ Preferences ▶ Graphic Options (ver 2025.0) ### Operation 1. Follow the location indicated in the section above. 2. Adjust the settings as needed: Show Shadow | Shows or hides Avatar shadows by default. ---|--- Use Shader | Sets whether or not the shader is used. The shader makes the shade of objects appear smoother. Use Normal Map | Set the Normal Map usage to realistically express the 3D Seamlines and texture of the fabric. ANTIALISING | Sets how smooth the outlines of objects appear. As the number increases, the outlines become smoother and the rendering speed becomes slower. Use VBOs | Set the VBOs usage in order to improve the rendering speed. Image Resolution Setting (ver. 2025.0) | Set the maximum image resolution for rendering. The Images that exceed the set resolution are downscaled only during rendering to optimize performance. The higher the image resolution, the more memory Marvelous Designer requires to render and process.
content_description: Customize your software experience by adjusting default settings in User Settings to align with your preferences for enhanced performance and usability.

title: [Mode] UV EDITOR
content: ### Objective To edit UV for mapping 2D textures on patterns. ### Location Window ▶ UV Editor (Ver. 2025.0) Viewport Title Bar ▶ Right-click Dropdown menu ▶ UV Editor (ver. 2025.0) UV Editor mode button on the toolbar at the top of the window. (up to Ver. 10) ### Operation Access the UV Editor from the Location above. Back and Side UV can be exported as UV. (Ver. 2025.0) #### [Definition of UV screen, coordination, and tiles] ![UV_Editor.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47437954503577) Horizontal axis: U Vertical axis: V A square of one U/ V: Tile UV snapshot saves each Tile as a single image. The coordinates of the tile are determined by the coordinates of U and V and are the same as the UV coordinates inside each tile on the image above. #### [Definition of Wire] ![UV_Editor_wire.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438003616537) Wire is the mesh line (Polygon) of UV. Wire image will be saved when saving UV. **Show UV Wire (Ver. 7.5)** **Location:** UV Editor Mode Popup menu (Right-click on background) Show Wire The existing textures are hidden and UV Wire (meshes) are displayed. **Rendering View Settings (ver. 9)** The toolbar contains rendering options. Diffuse, Metalness, Normal, Roughness Map. **View UV Maps (ver. 10)** 1. Upper left of the UV Editor window ▶ Click the View UV Map icon → Map icons that can be changed appear horizontally. 2. Click the desired map icon. → The UV of the 2D window changes to the type of map users click. ※Note: The UV map of the OBJ topstitch used in a garment is also provided. (ver. 11) View and Bake Displacement Map is now available (ver. 11) **Texture Repeat Type (ver. 10)/ Texture Mapping (ver. 11)** If the Texture Repeat Type of the fabric is set to Unified Map, changing the position of the UV in the UV Editor Window moves the textures in 2D and 3D patterns to the textures in the changed location. Fabric Properties | Description ---|--- Texture Repeat Type (ver. 10)/ Texture Mapping (ver. 11) | Unified Map (ver. 10) / Unified (ver. 11) | Display the texture based on the pattern layout of the UV map. [Repeat UV Settings] * Repeat U: Size the texture based on U direction. * Repeat V: Size the texture based on V direction. The number 1 means that the texture is repeated once between 0-1 of the UV map. **Move UV with Value (ver. 11)** 1. UV Editor Toolbar ▶ Click the Move UV tool. → Move UV window appears. 2. Set the distance to be moved. Distance 1 indicates the length of the segment of the UV Tile in the UV Editor window. 3. Move the UV by clicking the Arrow icon or pressing the directional keys on the keyboard. → UV is moved according to the distance you set.
content_description: This webpage serves as a comprehensive guide for accessing and utilizing the UV Editor in version 2025.0 to effectively map 2D textures onto patterns.

title: Quick Pinching /Advanced Pinching with Soft Selection (Ver. 2025.0)
content: ## Quick Pinching ### Objective Like the existing pinching feature, Quick Pinching allows for fast and simple pinching by pulling the mouse-picked point as a single point. ### Location Quick Pinching is automatically activated while simulation is running: * Quick Pinching (Q): It is executed by default when the simulation starts. * 3D Tool Bar ▶ Drop-Down Menu ▶ Quick Pinching (Ver. 2025.0) ![Selectmove.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438152064025) ![SelectQuickPinch.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438152167833) ![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438199330713) ## Advanced Pinching ### Objective Advanced Pinching is an evolved version of Quick Pinching that allows for precise pinching based on the user's desired area and fall-off settings. ### Location Advanced Pinching can be activated while simulation is running: * **Ver. 2025.0:** 3D Tool Bar ▶ Pinching Drop-Down Menu ▶ Advanced Pinching ![SelectAdvancedpinching2.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438152548121) * **Up to Ver. 2024.2:** 3D Background Context Menu (Right-click 3D background) ▶ Advanced Pinching (Shift + E) ### Operation (2025.0) 1. Load a garment into the scene. 2. Activate Simulation and select the Select/Move Tool ( Q ). 3. (With simulation active) Select Advanced Pinching from the Location above. 4. The Advanced Pinch Settings dialog window will pop up _(see images below)_ 5. In the Option section, adjust the following tool options to your preference: ### Operation (up to ver. 2024.2) 1. Load a garment into the scene. 2. Activate Simulation and select the Select/Move Tool ( Q ). 3. (With simulation active) Right-click the background in the 3D Window to bring up the 3D Background Context Menu. 4. Run the Advanced Pinch (Shift + E) option. 5. The Advanced Pinch Settings dialog window will pop up _(see images below)_ 6. In the Option section, adjust the following tool options to your preference: Range | The shape graph reflects the selected Falloff(Shape * Distance * Power) and cannot be manipulated directly. ---|--- Falloff Shape | Select the Falloff Shape: Bump or Linear ![falloff shape.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438138557465) Falloff Distance | Set the distance of the selection range to the radius: Min/max: 1-500(mm) ![Visual indicator of falloff distance.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438138699289) Falloff Power | A value that sets the strength of falloff. Min:-2.0 Max:+2.0 ![4869aa7f-745f-4861-a5c8-64257497e6bf.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438153202201) Options | Distance Measure | How the distance from the picking point is measured. Surface | When multiple layers of patterns are together, only one independent layer will be selected. Straight | Select all patterns within a certain distance from the picking point regardless of the layer selected. Distance Indicator | Indicates the Falloff Distance/Power values using 2 concentric circles around the pinch icon. When turned off the circles will disappear. ![78de1a69-72a1-4cc6-acc5-2031751e5df2.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438216650393) Limit to Selected Patterns | When selected only one pattern will be affected regardless of whether the Distance Measure is Surface or Straight. ![999a90e8-8b62-4bab-ae88-7a84bb454b03.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438167297049) Display Weights | Displays a contrasting color to the mesh where the weight value is applied. ![2d28e3ff-3eea-412a-a077-ee328038e99b.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438201394073) Modify the Range and Option values and freely pinch the patterns.
content_description: Discover the powerful Quick and Advanced Pinching features in Marvelous Designer, enabling efficient and precise garment adjustments during simulation.

title: Why do I have to pay tax?
content: **Question** I am VAT registered. Why do I have to pay tax? **Answer** Please note that if you have a correct registered VAT ID, you can add VAT ID on Billing Address and your tax will be waived Since January 2019, CLO Virtual Fashion LLC(Marvelous Designer US office) has officially been registered VAT MOSS(Sales Tax) in Ireland(EU). \- Since our online license sales are handled by our US office, all of our Individual license pricing will be in effect, according to the regulation below. From January 2015, new legislation came into force that affects the sale of digital services to customers in other EU countries. Digital services include broadcasting, telecommunications, and electronic services(which includes software products). The VAT rate that is calculated for this type of transaction is based on a place of supply the service. The legislation that is regulating MOSS rules is: * [Council Directive (EU) 2017/2455](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/PDF/?uri=CELEX:32017L2455&from=EN) \- supplies of services and distance sales of goods (VAT e-commerce package). * [Council Directive 2008/8/EC](http://eur-lex.europa.eu/LexUriServ/LexUriServ.do?uri=OJ:L:2008:044:0011:0022:EN:PDF) \- a place of supply of services. * [Council Implementing Regulation (EU) No 1042/2013](http://eur-lex.europa.eu/LexUriServ/LexUriServ.do?uri=OJ:L:2013:284:0001:0009:EN:PDF) \- place of supply of services. This means if your billing address is under the EU region, VAT rates for each country will be added to your purchase. Austria | 20% ---|--- Belgium | 21% Bulgaria | 20% Czech Republic | 21% Denmark | 25% Germany | 19% Estonia | 20% Ireland | 23% Greece | 24% Spain | 21% France | 20% Croatia | 25% Italy | 22% Cyprus | 19% Latvia | 21% Lithuania | 21% Luxembourg | 17% Hungary | 27% Malta | 18% Netherlands | 21% Poland | 23% Portugal | 23% Romania | 19% Slovenia | 22% Slovakia | 20% Finland | 24% Sweden | 25% UK | 20% If you would like to discover more regarding VAT MOSS, please review the file attached.
content_description: This web page provides essential information on VAT registration and compliance for digital service purchases, including guidance on tax exemptions for registered VAT IDs within the EU.

title: Add Pattern Thickness
content: ### ### Objective Extrude garment to express thickness. (These settings will apply to mesh export when using Thick export option, or use for 3D display only). ### Location 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern / Transform Pattern 3D Window ▶ Garment Display Option ▶ Wireframe on Monochrome (Thick) (ver. 2024.2) ### ### Operation (ver. 2024.2) 1. Follow the guideline below to set Garment Display Option to Wireframe on Monochrome (Thick). 3D Window ▶ Garment Display Option ▶ Wireframe on Monochrome (Thick) 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern / Transform Pattern 3. Select a Pattern or Pattern line to express doubled sided effect. → Its properties appear in the Property Editor. 4. Property Editor ▶ Geometry → Modifies the Geometry Properties which will affect mesh style / extrusion direction when exporting with thickness. #### Geometry Properties Add'l Thickness - Rendering (mm) | Displays the added thickness in addition to the Thickness value of Fabric Style. ---|--- Extrusion Direction | Sets the direction to display the thickness. Both | Apply the thickness front/rear around the pattern. Forward | Apply the thickness in the front direction of the pattern. Backward | Apply the thickness in the rear direction of the pattern. Toggle each side on or off to determine whether to generate the Mesh. (ver. 2025.0) Front Face | Set whether or not the front part is displayed based on the normal direction. Back Face | Set whether or not the back part is displayed based on the normal direction. Seam Face | Set whether or not to show overlapping sides on the sewn line. Side Geometry | Curvature (%) | Set side geometry lateral curvature percentage. Resolution | Set divisions for the side mesh. Double Side | Apply Curvature attribute values to both front and back symmetrical from the pattern. UV Expansion (ver. 2025.0) | The Side and Back UVs can be edited in UV Editor. [**Video here**](https://youtu.be/6e8yRsHUv_8) Back Face | Check this on to show the back face UV. Side Face | Check this on to show the side thickness UV. Mesh Style | Triangle | Re-mesh the pattern using triangular mesh option Quad (Optimized) | Re-mesh the pattern using quadrangular mesh option. Generates aligned automatic Retopology results. Quad (Grid) | Re-mesh the pattern using quadrangular mesh option. Generates pattern with a uniform grid. Face Count | Display total face count of the pattern. Vertex Count | Display total vertex count of the pattern. ※ Note: To use UV Expansion, Thick Textured surface must be active in the 3D window. ### Operation (Ver. 2024.1 and below) 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern / Transform Pattern 2. Select a Pattern or Pattern line to express doubled sided effect. → Its properties appear in the Property Editor. 3. Property Editor ▶ Selected Line ▶ Curved Side Geometry ▶ Check on Double Sided → The selected Pattern or Pattern line is now being displayed as double sided.
content_description: This web page provides detailed instructions for configuring garment thickness and mesh export settings in the 3D design software, enabling users to effectively visualize and manipulate garment properties.

title: Trims
content: ### Objective Modify existing Trims and apply them to garments with the following features. * Glue Trim * Tack on Trim * Delete Trim * Transform Trims * Set Trim Stiffness * Right-Click Options Menu * Trim Simulation Recording ※Note: * To learn how to import OBJ as Trim, please refer to articles [3D File (OBJ) Import/Export](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358223288601), [3D File (FBX) Import/Export](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358232885017) and [Trim Style Window (Ver. 2024.1)](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358161655705) * To Learn and modify Trim Properties, please refer to the [Trim Properties](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358187139609) page. * With the current versions, Trim Simulation with Collision only works with CPU Simulation. This does not work with GPU simulation at this time. * * * ## ## Glue Trim ### Objective Glue 3D Trims onto Garments and simulate together (ver 3.0.0). ### Operation #### Glue Trim 1. Click the loaded Trim with the Select/Move tool. → Gizmo for the selected OBJ appears. 2. Click on the Glue icon next to the OBJ Gizmo, then mouse over the desired location. → preview tags along the mouse. 3. Click on the desired location. → Selected trim automatically attaches to the place. 4. Use the Gizmo to adjust the position and angle. ※ Note: To cancel the arrangement, press Esc on the keyboard. 5. Activate Simulation. → Trim is now being simulated along with the rest of the Garments. ※Note: You can select multiple trims and move or rotate those by using Gizmo. (ver. 11 ) * * * ## Tack on Trim (ver. 2025.0) ### Objective Attach trims to desired locations on by using the tack tool to apply them to multiple points across and various patterns. ### Operation 1. Using **Select/Move** tool in the 3D toolbar, click ![Direct Positiong.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438151583513)**Direct Positioning** next to the Gizmo. 2. Hover over the pattern and click the desired location. 3. Using **Tack** tool in the 3D toolbar, Click on an initial point on the trim. 4. Click on the desired point on the garment. * Repeat the step to tack the trim to multiple points 5. Click the Simulate tool. ※Note: Tack is not available on deactivated trims. * * * ## Delete Trim ### Objective Delete selected Trims ### Operation 1. Select Trim in the 3D viewport 2. Click Delete key on Keyboard to remove. → Selected OBJ is now being removed from the Garments. 3. Delete trim can also be done through the right click options menu. * * * ## Transform Trims ### Objective Transform trim as needed. ### Operation #### Via the Scale Gizmo Click and drag on the X, Y, or Z-axis to transform the Trim. Axis | Description ---|--- X-Axis | The red axis of the Gizmo. Click and drag the x-axis to transform the trim along its x-axis. Y-Axis | The yellow-green axis of the Gizmo. Click and drag the y-axis to transform the trim along its y-axis. Z-Axis | The blue axis of the Gizmo. Click and drag the z-axis to transform the along its z-axis. Square | The yellow square located in the center of the Scale Gizmo. Click and drag the square to transform the trim, while maintaining its x, y, and z ratio. → The trim is transformed. When the trim transformation is complete, click the Scale button again. → The Gizmo used for moving and rotating trims appears. #### Via the Property Editor through [Trim Style Window](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358161655705) 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Window ▶ Trim 2. Select the trim style to be transformed. → The properties of the trim appear in the Property Editor. 3. Find the Scale option. 4. Enter the desired value for the below options. Option | Description ---|--- X-Axis | Enter the desired x-axis value. Y-Axis | Enter the desired y-axis value. Z-Axis | Enter the desired z-axis value. Maintain Ratio | Toggle this option on to adjust an OBJ while maintaining its x, y, and z ratio. * * * ## Set Trim Stiffness (ver. 2024.2) ### Objective Semi-Elastic Trim can be achieved when reducing stiffness value. ### Operation 1. Select Trim in the 3D window. 2. In the Property Editor, adjust Stiffness Value. → When Stiffness Value is reduced, the trim will be slightly bent when sufficient force is applied. → To get more rigid Trim simulation, increase the Stiffness Value. ※Note: The Stiffness of the trim can only be set when the trim material is in the "active" state. * * * ## Right-Click Menu ### Objective Set extra Trim Options include Trim Simulation toggles, Unglue, refresh Trim Textures and export selected Trim to USD layer. ### Operation 1. Select Trim in the 3D viewport. 2. Right-click on the selected Trim. → Trim is now being selected and Trim Options pop-up menu appears. #### Trim Options Select All Trims | Select all Trims in the 3D window. ---|--- Delete | Delete selected Trim. \- or use keyboard shortcut: Del Copy | Copy selected trim. \- or use keyboard shortcut: Ctrl + C Paste | Pasted copied trim. \- or use keyboard shortcut: Ctrl + V Simulation (ver. 2024.2) | Freeze | Freeze selected trims. \- Trim collides with garments but maintain the 3D position with no gravity influence. Activate | Activate simulation on selected trims. \- Trim collides with garments and influenced by weight and gravity. Deactivate | Deactivate selected trims. \- Trim does not collide with garments and maintains it’s 3D position. Unglue | Unglue trim from garment if glue function is applied. \- This option will not be available if glue function is not applied. Hide Trim | Hide selected trim or trims. Refresh Textures | Refresh selected trims textures. Export to USD Layer (ver. 12.1) | Export Trim to USD authoring layer, or create a new USD file with the selected trims. \- To learn more on USD export and USD layer editor in Marvelous Designer. Please move to [USD file Compatibility](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358343098777) page. ※Note: * To copy and paste multiple trims, hold down the Shift key on the keyboard and select all trims to be copied, then perform the procedure above. * When copying and pasting multiple trims, they must all be placed within a Pattern. * * * ### Trim Simulation Recording (Ver. 2025.0) When recording garment animation, the simulation cache of the Trim is recorded a separate layer from the Pattern, under the descendant of the Garment Layer.
content_description: This webpage aims to provide comprehensive guidance on modifying and applying various trims to garments in 3D design, including operations for gluing, tacking, deleting, transforming trims, and utilizing simulation features.

title: How to Update to the Latest Version
content: *If you're using a subscription license (Enterprise / Personal / Student), you all have access to download the latest version of Marvelous Designer. *If you updated your version to 12, you can also download the version on [my account](https://www.marvelousdesigner.com/mypage). ### STEP 1 On your computer, sign in with your account ( your End User ID) on [the website](https://www.marvelousdesigner.com/mypage). ### ### STEP 2 On my account page, you will see the "Download" button. ### ### STEP 3 Click > Download > Select MD 12 at the top. ![mceclip1.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47437972109337) ## Why keep Marvelous Designer updated? If you're using a subscription license, we will always provide access to the latest version of the software. Our development team is constantly at work to further develop new feature, and add improvements within each version release (including patches) in order to support our users' work. This will maintain stability and efficiency in the software. Updating Marvelous Designer to the latest version or patch version allows you to take advantage of the latest features and bug fix updates, to keep Marvelous Designer running at it's best efficiency. ## Check out the latest features and updates <https://www.marvelousdesigner.com/learn/newfeature>

title: Marvelous Designer File Format
content: ### Marvelous Designer File Format Type | Format | Description ---|---|--- Garment | [*.zpac](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358279381529) | Contains information on Garments, Patterns, Sewing, and Fabrics. Project | [*.zprj](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358219651225) | Compresses the various files used for Garment creation into one file, and saves it. The Project file contains the AVT file that has Avatar-related data [Avatar, Accessories, Arrangement Bounding Volumes, Arrangement Points, Avatar size, Poses] and the ZPac file that contains Garment-related data [3D Garments, 2D Patterns, Fabrics, subsidiary Material], as well as an animation file if there is animation. Avatar | [*.avt](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358359735961) | Contains all the information related to Avatars (Model, Sizing data, Poses, Motions, Accessories, Bounding Volumes, Arrangement Points). Avatar (Encrypted) | [*.avte](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358187017113) | Encrypted MD/CLO avatar file types. This file type cannot be exported,[ This includes the Metahuman Body Types found in the Avatar folders. ](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358187017113) Pose | [*.pos](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358350508697) | Avatar Pose information that, automatically saved whenever the Garment is saved. The Avatar’s Pose can easily be changed with this file. Avatar Poses from other software can only be saved when the Avatar is a COLLADA file with joints. Joint Motion | [*.mtn](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358363172249) | Contains Avatar Motion information. As with the Pose file, can only be saved on COLLADA file Avatars with joint and Animation information. Fabric | [*.zfab](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358267968153) | Contains the property values (texture + physical properties) of the set Fabric. Physical Property | [*.psp](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358434392857) | Contains the detailed values of Fabric Physical Properties. Topstitch | [*.sst](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358389918873) | Contains the type, number of lines, thread thickness, SPI, length, etc. Button | [*.btn](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358452715161) | Contains the type, size, and color of Buttons. Buttonhole | [*.bth](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358452715161) | Contains the tyle, size, and color of the Buttonholes. Arrangement Point | [*.arr](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358280634905) | Arrangement Points are the blue points that are distributed around the Avatar, and are used to arrange Patterns easily around the Avatar. Arrangement Points are created on top of the Arrangement Bounding Volume covering the surroundings of the Avatar. Arrangement Bounding Volume | [*.pan](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358365447705) | Arrangement Bounding Volumes are the green cylinders covering each part of the Avatar, and each end of a cylinder is connected to an Avatar’s joint. As such, even if the Avatar’s Pose is changed, the cylinder simply adjusts to the changed Pose and can be used as it is. Tape Measure | *.mea | It has the information of the tape measure created in the avatar. Camera Projection | *.cmp | Contains the camera's Field of View information (near, far, etc.). Camera Transformation | *.cmt | Contains camera view information of the 3D Garment window. Simulation Property | [*.smp](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358232630937) | Contains settings for Simulation.
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide to the various file formats used in Marvelous Designer, detailing their specific purposes and the information they contain for garment creation and avatar management.

title: Object Browser
content: ### Objective View and edit items used in both 3D and 2D Windows such as Scene, Fabric, Button, Buttonhole, Topstitch, and Puckering. ### Operation ※ Note: Show or hide the Object Browser by clicking Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ Window ▶ Object Browser (Show) Scene | Scene tab is the primary, fastest, and most streamlined tool for finding or selecting object. It lets you quickly review a list of all objects and its structure in the 3D and 2D Windows. The list is in the order of object created, but when you click on Name, the object list is sorted A to Z (1 to 10). Click and drag to [reorder](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360000489708) Fabric styles as desired (ver4.1.0). Button | Button Tab displays a list of button items. title: Trim Style Window (Ver. 2024.1)
content: ### ### ### Objective Manage Trims as a shape or style in the Trim Window. It is possible to create, copy, apply, and set a style in the Trim list window. ### Location Object Browser ▶ Trim (Ver. 2025.0) Main Menu ▶ Object Browser ▶ Trim (Ver. 2025.0) Main Menu ▶ Window ▶ Trim (up to 2024.2) Window Dropdown Menu ▶ Trim (up to 2024.2) ![ObjectBrowser-Trim.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438283062553) ### Operation #### Add & Apply one or more Trim Styles 1\. Click Add at the top right to load a file to use as Trim. or Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import and import a file. In the popup window, choose Object Type as Trim. or drag and drop a file (from Library or File Explorer) directly to the Trim Style Window. **→** A Trim style is added. 2\. Drag the style from the Trim window to the 3D window, apply it, and Glue. #### Copy & Paste 1\. Select the added Trim style and click the Copy button. **→** The selected Trim style is copied. 2\. Click the Delete button on the right side of the Trim style that is not applied to the 3D window. **→** The selected Trim style is deleted. #### Change Trim Styles 1\. Use the Select/Move tool to select a trim in the 3D window. 2\. Click the ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438253617561) Assign button to the right of the trim style name. Or drag and drop a Trim style onto the trim you've selected. **→** The selected Trim's style has been changed. 3\. Right-click on Trim to Delete / Delete all Unused Trims / Rename (Ver. 2025.0). **Trim Windo****w****(up to Ver. 2024.2)** Add | Allows you to import files to use as trims into the Trim Window. Supported file formats include .TRM, .OBJ, .FBX, .USD ---|--- Copy | Makes a copy of the highlighted/selected Trim file Assign | Apply or replace trim shapes/styles onto existing trims as desired. Delete Unused | Removes from the Trim window any unused Trim files. ※ Note: [The default file format for Trim in Marvelous Designer is .TRM file. Other supported file formats for importing Object Types as trim include .OBJ, .FBX, and .USD.](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358232885017)
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for managing and applying trim styles within the Trim Window of Marvelous Designer, detailing operations such as adding, copying, and modifying trim shapes and styles.

title: Puckering Style Window (2025.0)
content: ### Objective Adds Puckering Styles and controls their properties. ### Location Object Browser ▶ Puckering Style Tab (ver. 2025.0) Main Menu ▶ Window ▶ Object Browser ▶ Puckering Style Tab (ver. 2025.0) ### ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438120178585) ### Operation #### Open Asset Library 1. Open the Asset Library tab in Location. 2. Select the ![Asset Library.svg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/54024056899481) Asset Library icon to open the default location for Puckering assets in the New Library Window. #### Add New Puckering Style & Apply 1. Select the tool/menu indicated. 2. Click "+Add" in the Object Browser. Or add a Puckering file (.PTP) by dragging it to the Puckering tab or on the Puckering asset. → A Puckering style is added. #### Copy Puckering Style & Apply 1. Click Copy at the top right. → A Puckering style is duplicated. 2. Replace an existing Puckering Style and apply it. Or after selecting the Puckering first, click the Assign button to the right of the Puckering style. → The Puckering Style is replaced. #### Assign New Puckering Style 1. title: Edit UV
content: ### Objective Check patterns' UVs before exporting garments and edit UV by shifting pattern locations in the UV Editor (ver2.3.0). ### Location Main Menu ▶ Window ▶ UV Editor (2025.0) Viewport Title Bar ▶ Right-click Dropdown menu ▶ UV Editor (2025.0) Object Browser ▶ UV Editor (up to 2024.2) ![Captura](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438249522713) ### ### Operation #### Manual 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Window ▶ UV Editor Object Browser ▶ UV Editor → A dotted rectangular guideline appears around all patterns in the UV Editor. 2. Click the icon image at the top-right corner of the guideline. → The guideline icon changes and it becomes available to adjust the UV area manually. → Guidelines display repetitively (ver2.4.0). 3. Click and drag the edge of scale guide to resize the UV area as wanted. 4. Select and shift patterns accordingly. #### Automatic If manually edited by clicking the icon to switch over to automatic. → The dotted rectangular guideline re-appears around all the patterns in the UV Editor.

title: Library Window
content: Starting from **Marvelous Designer 2025.2** , the Library(Legacy) window has been integrated into the **New Library** window and is no longer available. 📒[**New Library Manual**](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358127622809-New-Library-Window-2025-0) * * * ### Objective Conveniently manage and open files in the program using the Library Window. Add frequently used folders to the Library to easily open files: drag and drop a file from the registered folder into the 3D Window or with the left mouse button, double click the file. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Window ▶ Library Side Panel Title Bar ▶ Right-click Drop Down Menu ▶ Library (Ver. 2025.0) ### Operation #### Icon Menus (Top/Bottom) - Library Window Download (Ver. MD10) | Download the newly added default files as a whole. Selectively download files from the folder with the "N" sign. ---|--- Reset | Reset registered folders in the Library. Add Folder | Add frequently used folders to the Library. Refresh | Apply any changes made in the Library such as deleting or adding folders. Select All (Downloadable Items Only) | If you activate a checkbox on the top left corner of downloadable items, the 'Select All' button will appear where the Refresh button used to be. A single selection will select the entire downloadable items, and clicking the button again will deselect all. List / Icon | Toggle between different views. (ver2.3.0) Search | Use Search to locate files quickly and efficiently within the Library.(ver3.0.0) #### Right Mouse Button Menus - Library Window Click the RMB on the folders at the top or bottom of the Library window to access the menus below. Delete | Delete the bookmarked folder. ---|--- Rename | Renaming the bookmark folder. The name of the original folder saved on the computer will not be changed. Show in Explorer (Ver. 12.1) | Open the explorer window where the bookmarked folder or the selected folder and files are located. Add to Workspace | Add the corresponding item to the workspace ※ Note: Hover over the desired Project/Garment file thumbnail to preview font, back, and side views.
content_description: This web page serves as a guide to effectively utilize the newly integrated New Library window in Marvelous Designer 2025.2 for managing and accessing your files efficiently.

title: Apply Texture
content: ### Objective Apply 2D image files to express the surface texture of fabric. ### Operation #### Via Drag and Drop 1. Open a folder that contains the desired texture image in your file browser. 2. Drag and drop the texture image onto a pattern in the 2D or 3D window. → The texture of all patterns using the same Fabric will have the new texture applied. ※ Note: * If a texture image is already applied, the existing texture image will be replaced when applying a new texture image via drag and drop. * Drag and drop an image file directly from the file browser to the Open icon next to the Texture menu in the Property Editor (Ver. 4.0.0). * Drag and drop an image file directly from the file browser to an object in the program, then select the correct map: texture, normal, specular (Ver. 4.0.0). * After Base Color Texture image is applied, maps for Displacement, Opacity, Roughness, and Metalness channel can be automatically generated using PBR Map Generator (ver. 2024.1). * If using a Base Color Map with an alpha (to transmit transparency) and Opacity Map are applied at the same time, the alphas of both are reflected in the transparency result (ver.2024.1) * Before (Ver. 2024.1) when the Base Color Map and Opacity Map were applied at the same time: only the alpha of the Opacity Map was reflected in the transparency expression, not the alpha of the Basecolor Map. Now the alpha of both maps is applied (Ver. 2024.1) * You can now "open your Texture File with Another App" (this is found under Property editor ▶ material ▶ Base color ▶ base color map ▶ ellipsis (**...**) for quick editing (Ver. 2025.0) #### Via Property Editor * Select a Fabric to apply a texture image to from the Fabric tab in the Object Browser. * Follow the path: Property Editor ▶ Fabric ▶ Texture Open button. → The Open File window appears. * Find and select the desired texture image from the file browser, then load. → The selected texture image is now applied to the Fabric.
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for applying 2D image files to enhance the surface texture of fabrics in both 2D and 3D environments through intuitive drag-and-drop functionality and detailed property editor options.

title: Seam Taping
content: Create Seam Taping Extend Seam Taping Seam Taping Physical Properties ![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438276828825) ## ## Create Seam Taping ### Objective Reinforce edges of Patterns to withstand from drooping down by gravity when Simulating. ### Location 2D Toolbar ▶ Seam Taping Select Segment Pattern ▶ Property Editor ▶ Selected Line ▶ Seam Taping ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: 2D Toolbar ▶ Seam Taping Select Pattern Segment ▶ Property Editor ▶ Selected Line ▶ Seam Taping 2. Select a segment Pattern to reinforce. → The selected segment is now being highlighted in orange color. 3. Activate the Simulate. → The seam tape is now being applied to the selected segment and being reinforced. ※ Note: * Click-and-drag also allows applying seam tapes. * When the Seam Taping tool is active, the applied seam tape is color coded with arrows indicating the direction of applied seam tape (ver. 2024.2). ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438288340249) ![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438276828825) ## Extend Seam Tapping (Ver. 2024.2) ### Objective Edit the seam tape extension output with options for overlapped and non-overlapped structures when 2 or more seam taping are intersected can be created. (Example: To create non-overlapped seam taping, first seam taping stop on the outline; second seam taping stop on the 1st seam taping) ### Location 2D Toolbar ▶ Seam Taping Select Seam Taping ▶ Property Editor ▶ Selected Line ▶ Extend ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: 2D Toolbar ▶ Seam Taping Select Seam Taping ▶ Property Editor ▶ Selected Line ▶ Extend 2. Use the drop-down menu to select the stop position options: None, To Outline, and To Seam Taping. * * **Extend (None)** = Does not extend. * **Extend (To Outline)** = Extend to the pattern outline * **Extend (To Seam Taping)** = Extends to the seam taping area of ​​the intersected line. ※ Note: The arrow direction indicate the direction of seam taping. The end without arrow tip is the start of seam taping. And the end with arrow tip is the end of the seam taping. ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438288569497) ![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438276828825) ## Seam Taping Physical Properties ### Location 2D Toolbar ▶ Seam Taping Select Seam Taping ▶ Property Editor ▶ Selected Line ▶ Physical Property ### Operation Physical Property | Fabric or Elastic ---|--- Preset | Select default presets from the dropdown menu: * Fusible (common) * Fusible (lapel) * Fusible (nonwoven) * Fusible (nonwoven_Small Parts) * Reinforcement (Bone Pocket) * Reinforcement (Under Collar) * Custom (see Detail) Use the folder icon to open the file explorer. Use the Save icon to save a custom made property. Detail | Depending on Fabric or Elastic options, you can adjust the additional Material simulation properties based on specific material property sliders.
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to provide a comprehensive guide on creating, extending, and managing seam taping in pattern design, ensuring enhanced structural integrity and simulation accuracy.

title: Offset as Internal Line
content: ### Objective Input specific measurements to offset Patterns and segments as Internal Lines. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Pattern/ Transform Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern/ Transform Pattern ### Operation #### Offset as Internal Line 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Pattern/ Transform Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern/ Transform Pattern 2. Right-click on top of a Pattern and select Offset As Internal Line from the pop-up menu. → The Offset as Internal Line window appears. 3. Configure the settings as needed. Number of Offsets | Set the number of Internal Lines to be generated ---|--- Distance | Set the interval between each Internal Line. All | Set the distance of all segments to be the same. Individual (Ver. 2025.0) | Set the spacing for each line segment individually. Offset From (Ver. 2025.0) | When inputting individual distances, the individual line can be set as the previous or selected line. Reverse Direction | Change in the reverse direction of the selected segment. Both Sides (Ver. 2025.0) | Create internal lines in both directions based on the selected segment. Extend | to Pattern Outline | Extend to Pattern Outline. to Internal Line | Extend to Internal Line of the pattern. 4. Click OK. → Depending on the settings, the internal line/shape is created. → If it is a curve, the curve point is automatically optimized. #### Offset as Internal Line along Curved (ver3.2.0) 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Pattern/ Transform Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern/ Transform Pattern 2. Select the two Pattern outlines between where the Internal Lines are created. 3. Right click on the selected Pattern outline and select Offset as Internal Line along Curved (ver3.2.0) → The Offset as Internal Line along Curved (ver3.2.0) 4. Adjust the options below as needed, then select OK. Name | Description ---|--- Number of Offsets | Set the number of Internal Lines to be created. Offset | Set the distance between each Internal Lines. Distance to Segment Edge | Set the distance from the Pattern outlines for the Internal Lines. Reverse Direction | Horizontally reverse the Internal Lines' position based on the Distance to Segment Edge. Opposite Segment | Vertically reverse the Internal Lines' position based on the Distance to Segment Edge. Straight Line | Create Internal Lines as straight lines. Perpendicular Direction | Create Internal Lines perpendicular to the selected Pattern outlines. → Internal Lines are created based on the above settings. ※ Note: * Using the same function, additional Internal Lines can be created between Internal Lines. * When the Pattern outlines or Internal Lines are divided in multiple segments, hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to select them all.
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for users to input measurements and create offset patterns as internal lines within a 2D pattern design tool.

title: Buttonhole Style Property (Ver. 2025.0)
content: ### Objective Use these options to edit buttonhole styles and materials. **** ### Location Main Menu ▶ Window ▶ Object Browser ▶ Buttonhole **Viewport** Title Bar ▶ Right-click Dropdown menu ▶ Object Browser ▶ Buttonhole ### Operation Object Browser ▶ Select a buttonhole item in the Buttonhole Tab. → The properties are displayed in the Property Editor. Properties | Description ---|--- Information | Name | Enter a name of the Buttonhole. Shape | Select the type of the buttonhole from the drop down icon. Click the plus icon to[ register the Buttonhole as OBJ file](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358452715161). Width (mm) | Decide the width of the buttonhole by millimeters. Material Button / Thread | Type | Set the appropriate material for the Buttonhole. Base Color | Color | Select the color of the base color. Displacement Map | Click the explore button and apply a texture image from Library/Folder, generate with the generate icon. Amount | Adjust the maximum height of the displacement map. The white area of the displacement map shows the maximum height. Shift | Adjust the distance between the displacement map and the garment surface Clipping | Adjust to delete all geometries below the Clipping value. Particle Distance | Adjust the Particle Distance of newly created meshes. Keep Continuity | Extend the adjacent face to eliminate the boundary line. ※ Note: Only applicable to Welded OBJs. Opacity | Opacity | Adjust the opacity level from 0 to 100. Opacity Map | RGB Mode | The encoded map with alpha value in RGB channel. Alpha Mode | The encoded map with alpha value in alpha channel. Reflection | Roughness | Dropdown menu | Intensity | Edit fabric gloss by adjusting Intensity of the Roughness slider Map | Edit fabric gloss by adding and modifying Roughness Map. Map | Select the Browse button next to the Map option to add a Roughness Map to the selected Fabric style. or generate a custom map Map Intensity | Adjust the Map's Intensity. The range of Roughness map intensity was enlarged in (ver. 2024.2) Invert | Select to invert the gloss of the fabric. When this option is selected, the shinny part becomes dull and vice-versa. To use Specular Maps provided in below ver. 6, check this option. Reflection Intensity | The greater/lesser the Reflection Intensity value is, the more reflective/dull the material or fabric is. Metalness | Adjust metallic level. Higher value makes the surface more metallic. Metalness Map | Partially express metallics using a grayscale image. The white parts of the map appear metallic.
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for editing buttonhole styles and materials, allowing users to customize properties such as shape, width, and texture for enhanced garment design.

title: Property Editor
content: ### ### Objective Edit a selected asset or style group's properties in the Property Editor. ### Location Side Panel Title Bar ▶ Right-click Dropdown menu (ver. 2025.0) ### Operation #### Property Editor Pattern Property | Shows a pattern’s property on the Property Editor when it is selected ---|--- Internal Shape Property | Shows an internal shape’s property on the Property Editor when it is selected. Sewing Property | Shows a sewing line's property on the Property Editor when it is selected. Stitch Property | Shows a stitch's property on the Property Editor when it is selected. Fabric Property | Shows a pattern’s property on the Property Editor when it is selected from the fabric list. Button Property | Shows a button’s property on the Property Editor when it is selected. Buttonhole Property | Shows a buttonhole’s property on the Property Editor when it is selected. Avatar Property | Shows the pattern-related properties of an avatar on the Property Editor when it is selected. Simulation Property | Shows the simulation properties on the Property Editor. Right-click on the 3D Pattern Window and select Simulation Property from the pop-up menu. Wind Property | Shows the wind properties on the Property Editor. Right-click on the 3D Pattern Window and select Wind Property from the pop-up menu. 2D Window Property | Shows the 2D Pattern Window properties on the Property Editor. Right-click on the 2D Pattern Window and select 2D Pattern Window Property from the pop-up menu. #### #### Simulation Property 1. Follow and select the menu as below. Right-click Pop-Up Menu (on 3D Window) ▶ Simulation Properties → Open, save, and edit properties related to Simulation in the Property Editor. ※ Note: * Select All with Same Property: Right-click Pop-Up Menu (on 2D Patterns) ▶ Select All with Same Property ▶ Particle Distance/ Layer/ Fabric → Patterns with the same property is selected.
content_description: This web page provides guidance on editing the properties of various assets and style groups using the Property Editor in the 2025.0 version interface.

title: History Window
content: ### Objective Keep track of your workflow with the History window and revert to previous points at any given time. In addition, save 3D states to review and compare specific points of progress. ### Location #### History Window Side Panel Title Bar ▶ Right-click Dropdown menu (ver. 2025.0) #### Main Menu ▶History #### #### 3D State History Window ▶ 3D State Side Panel Title Bar ▶ Right-click Dropdown menu ▶ History Window ▶ 3D State (ver. 2025.0) Delete & Rename Right-click dropdown Menu (on 3D State) ▶ Delete or Rename ### Operation #### 3D State 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: History Window ▶ 3D State 2. Double click the desired 3D State. → Warning as follows appears: "Loading the 3D State will delete the current History. Would you like to proceed?" 3. Select OK. → The 3D garment is reverted to the selected 3D State. #### Delete & Rename 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right-click Pop-Up Menu (on 3D State) ▶ Delete or Rename → The name field is highlighted and name can be changed. → The selected 3D State is deleted. ※ You can find a preview window if hovering your mouse over the thumbnail of a desired '3D State' file. (ver. 12.2)
content_description: This web page provides guidance on using the History window and 3D State features to effectively track and manage your workflow, allowing you to revert to previous points and save specific 3D garment states for comparison.

title: Create Line (Avatar) / 3D Pen (Avatar)
content: ### Objective Draw lines on an Avatar and extract Patterns. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Line (Avatar) / 3D Pen (Avatar) (ver. 2025.0) 3D Toolbar ▶ Line (Avatar) / 3D Pen (Avatar) (ver. 2025.0) ### Operation 1. Follow the path indicated in the Location section. → If there is a Garment on the Avatar, the Garment appears translucent. 2. Hover the mouse over the Avatar. → A black dot follows the mouse. 3. Click on the desired position on the Avatar to create lines or shapes. → The lines or shapes appear on the Avatar in black. 4. Click on the start point to complete drawing the line. → The lines or shapes are created on the Avatar. **Updated 2025.1** Press **P** to switch between creating point within the 3D space or on the avatar. ※ Note: * To create a curve point while drawing lines on the Avatar, hold down the Ctrl key on the keyboard and click on the Avatar. * Hit the Delete key on the keyboard to cancel the latest action or hit the Esc key or Ctrl+Z to cancel all actions. * All lines and shapes drawn on the Avatar are saved when you save the file in Project, Garment, or Avatar file format.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for drawing lines and shapes on an Avatar using the 3D Garment feature, enabling users to extract patterns effectively.
